newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares hit new record, seen firming further.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares hit new record, seen firming further.

text.p: Russian shares closed at record highs on Monday, and traders predicted prices would remain firm.
The President's Day market holiday in the U.S. did not affect market activity, with demand maintaining earlier levels.
The Russian Trading System 24-share index rose 2.18 percent to a record 320.34 on a total market volume of $34.4 million, according to data from the NAUFOR brokers association.
Traders said that they do not expect a correction in the market in the near future, despite successive record highs on the RTS index.
"For now, I see only buying. There's no reason for a correction, even though the market is overheating," UFG trader Maxim Perlin said.

"Support today was very good, and there was real demand. People are now feeling very comfortable in the market. They understand the market is stabilising and prices are consolidating," Deutsche Morgan Grenfell chief trader Pavel Gronbjerg said.
Utility UES share prices edged up to $0.2164 from $0.2100 at the close on Friday and Surgutneftegaz rose to $0.711 from $0.685.
Rostelekom which was rated BB- by Standard & Poor's on Friday ahead of its planned Eurobond, rose to $4.12 from $4.02. The company said it plans to seek further ratings.
Traders said Rostelekom could be poised for considerable growth due to the rating.
Gazprom, which said it would fight a scheme by Regent Fund to set up a fund investing in domestic Gazprom shares, eased to $0.485 from $0.486.
Traders said the market for less liquid shares was not as active today as on Friday. The RTS-2 market for less liquid shares was stable, despite demand from western traders.
